parameters.content:
## Goodmedias Hub manual send POST JSON to this webhook. The workflow sends it through the **Send Email** (SMTP) node, then answers with the JSON the hub expects. ### 1. Credentials (required before publish) - **Header Auth**, name exactly `Goodmedias Webhook Secret` - Header name: `X-Webhook-Secret` - Header value: the same value as `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the hub - **SMTP**, name exactly `Goodmedias SMTP` - The SMTP account must be allowed to send as `from.email` ### 2. URLs - Test: `https:///webhook-test/goodmedias/manual-send` - Production (set `N8N_MANUAL_SEND_URL` to this): `https:///webhook/goodmedias/manual-send` Click **Listen for test event** before calling the test URL. **Publish** the workflow before calling the production URL. ### 3. Body the hub sends ```json { "idempotencyKey": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111", "requestedAt": "2026-10-12T15:00:00.000Z", "from": { "email": "alex@goodmedias.com", "name": "Alex" }, "to": { "email": "sam@contoso.com", "name": "Sam" }, "subject": "Quick question", "bodyText": "Hi Sam", "bodyHtml": "

Hi Sam

", "thread": { "threadId": "thread_demo" } } ``` `bodyHtml`, `from.name`, `to.name`, and `thread.threadId` are optional. A flat test body also works: `{ "from": "a@x.com", "to": "b@y.com", "subject": "Hi", "text": "Hello" }`. ### 4. Success response `{ "ok": true, "status": "sent", "idempotencyKey", "providerMessageId", "threadId" }` SMTP does not set `In-Reply-To` or `References`, so each send is a new message rather than a threaded reply.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, status: 'sent', idempotencyKey: $('Prepare Email').item.json.idempotencyKey, providerMessageId: $json.messageId || ('<' + $('Prepare Email').item.json.idempotencyKey + '@goodmedias>'), threadId: $('Prepare Email').item.json.threadId }) }}
